content.overview: Section 10A requires a company having a share capital to file a declaration of commencement of business and verify receipt of the value of shares agreed to be taken by subscribers before commencing business or exercising borrowing powers. Non-compliance attracts penalties and may lead to striking off.
content.glance: State the declaration and subscription-money requirements under s. 10A; note the bar on commencing business or borrowing until compliance; state the consequences of default.
content.study: Section 10A regulates commencement of business for companies with share capital. A company shall not commence any business or exercise any borrowing powers unless a declaration is filed by a director that every subscriber has paid the value of shares agreed to be taken, and the company has filed verification of its registered office. Failure to comply may result in penalties and, if no business is commenced for a prolonged period, possible striking off. Current-law framing: ground the analysis in s. 10A and the connected registered-office provision under s. 12.

sections.heading: Declaration of Subscription Money
sections.body: A director must file a declaration that every subscriber to the memorandum has paid the value of the shares agreed to be taken by him.

sections.heading: Registered Office Verification
sections.body: The company must also file verification of its registered office as required under the Act.

sections.heading: Bar on Business and Borrowing
sections.body: Until compliance, the company shall not commence business or exercise borrowing powers.

sections.heading: Consequences of Default
sections.body: Penalties apply; prolonged non-commencement may support striking-off action.

examples.title: Compliant commencement
examples.body: The company files the s. 10A declaration and registered-office verification. It may then commence business and borrow.

examples.title: Borrowing before declaration
examples.body: A company borrows before filing the s. 10A declaration. The borrowing is in breach of the statutory bar.

hypotheticals.question: Can a company with share capital start trading immediately after the certificate of incorporation?
hypotheticals.analysis: Not until the s. 10A declaration and registered-office verification are filed.

hypotheticals.question: Does s. 10A apply to companies limited by guarantee without share capital?
hypotheticals.analysis: Section 10A is directed at companies having a share capital.

distinctions.title: Incorporation (s. 7) vs commencement of business (s. 10A)
distinctions.left: Company becomes a body corporate on registration
distinctions.right: Additional compliance before starting business or borrowing

misconceptions.trap: The certificate of incorporation alone authorises commencement of business.
misconceptions.correction: Section 10A requires a further declaration and office verification before business or borrowing.

misconceptions.trap: Section 10A is only a formality with no consequence.
misconceptions.correction: Non-compliance attracts penalties and may lead to striking off for prolonged inaction.

cases.name: Salomon v. A. Salomon & Co. Ltd.
cases.facts: Properly incorporated company challenged as indistinct from controller.
cases.ratioDecidendi: Registered company is a separate legal person.
cases.relevance: Already in file; s. 10A operates after incorporation under ss. 7 and 9.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 10A problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Identify whether the company has share capital. II. Check declaration and office verification. III. Test any business or borrowing against the bar. IV. State consequences. V. Conclude.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What should submissions contain?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Filing status under s. 10A; timing; any business or borrowing; penalty exposure; precise relief.

examTips: Distinguish incorporation from commencement of business.
State the bar on business and borrowing.
